steps.prompt: In the last days before a big test, is it better to learn something new or to go over what you know? Why?

cards.title: Light review, not cramming
cards.body: In the final week, stop learning new topics. Keep the daily review going, redo a few error-log problems, and read your fact sheets once more. The Light review on the Math page is a short, untimed set of facts you already know: use it to warm up on the days before the test.

cards.title: Confidence comes from evidence
cards.body: Look back at your first mock and your latest one: the score, the blanks, the careless slips. You have done three full mocks, fifteen unit checks and hundreds of problems. Nerves are normal; they mean your brain is ready to work.

cards.title: Worked example: a quick fact
cards.problem: How many diagonals does a hexagon have?

steps.text: Each corner joins $3$ others by a diagonal.

try.prompt: How many diagonals from one corner?

steps.text: $\frac{6 \times 3}{2} = 9$, since each diagonal has two ends.
